transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess… I just don’t have much push anymore. I used to go to choir, do quilting, visit folks. Now most days I just sit home with the TV on low, even when I know people are expecting me.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, months, or longer?
Longer, I guess. It’s been sort of building since I retired from the school office… a little over two years ago.
Have you or anyone close to you noticed changes in your memory or ability to think clearly, like forgetting appointments, misplacing things, or having trouble following conversations?
I don’t know… not really. I mean, I forget little things sometimes, but I figure that’s just normal. I haven’t noticed anything big with conversations or such.

Over these past two years, would you say you've felt this low and lacking motivation nearly every day, or has it come and gone in separate stretches with periods where you felt more like your usual self in between?

It’s more… most days, I suppose. I don’t really have that push like I used to—for choir or quilting or going to see people. I just end up home with the TV low, even when I know folks are expecting me.
Besides feeling low on motivation, have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite over these past two years?
I haven’t really kept track. Sleep’s… maybe not as good some nights, but I don’t know. Appetite seems about the same, I guess.
During this time, have you ever felt worthless, excessively guilty, or had thoughts that life isn't worth living?
I don’t know… I don’t think like that much. I get down on myself some, I guess, but… I wouldn’t say all that.
During these past two years of feeling low, has there ever been a stretch of at least two weeks where your mood or lack of motivation felt noticeably worse than your usual baseline?

I don’t know if there was a clear two-week stretch. It’s more just been… most days I don’t have much push, like with choir or quilting or going visiting. I end up staying home with the TV on, even when I know people thought I’d come.
